title: The Natural History Museum to reopen hidden gallery closed since World War II
summary: The Natural History Museum has announced it will be throwing open the doors to a gallery which has been closed to the public since 1943. The gallery will initially reopen for 18 months on 16 September with Nature and Us, supported by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), where visitors can explore our evolving relationship with the natural world through 50 remarkable objects. Key specimens and historic objects appearing in Nature and Us include a miniature model of a Crystal Palace dinosaur, illustrating how early scientists and artists imagined prehistoric life; Jenny, a Victorian skeleton of a monk seal that reveals how wild animals were once exploited for entertainment; a bryozoan-encrusted Star Wars toy from the 1980s, showing how everyday objects can acquire new meanings through nature and time; and a 400,000-year-old handaxe whose discovery transformed our understanding of when humans first existed. title: MASI Lugano hosts first major posthumous retrospective of Kaari Upson
summary: MASI Lugano presents the first major posthumous retrospective dedicated to the American artist Kaari Upson (1970-2021). Upson, who gained traction in Europe after taking part in the 58th Venice Biennale (2019), is one of the most intense and original voices of her generation. In a career that lasted just over fifteen years, and spanned sculpture, video, drawing and installation, she constructed a layered language that she used to explore themes such as relationships, the body, illness and loss. Her works - suspended between intimacy and alienation - evoke an unsettling universe, in that everyday objects and environments become repositories for obsession and trauma. Although her art is rooted in her lived experience and her hometown of San Bernardino, California, it channels an intimate yet universal vision of the contemporary psyche. The exhibition at MASI takes in her entire oeuvre and is structured in five broadly chronological sections

title: Mondrian's defining masterpiece Composition III to be presented in Christie's 20/21 Evening Sale in London
summary: Christie's announces that Piet Mondrian's Composition III will be one of the key highlights of its 20th/21st Century: London Evening Sale on 14 October 2026 during Frieze Week. Carrying an estimate of £20,000,000-30,000,000, this masterwork is the most important Mondrian offered at auction in Europe since 2009, when Composition avec bleu, rouge, jaune et noir (1922) and Composition I (1920) were sold at Christie's Paris from the Collection of Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé. Composition III comes to auction for the first time, with past custodians including the legendary architect and collector of Modernism Armand P. Bartos and his wife Celeste. Painted in 1920, Composition III dates to a pivotal moment in the artist's career, as he achieved the first breakthrough examples of his visionary Neo-Plastic style. title: Nye & Company to auction Stradling Study Collection of American ceramics
summary: Nye & Company Auctioneers invites collectors, dealers, designers and connoisseurs everywhere to discover two days of exceptional objects at its Chic & Antique Auction, slated for September 9th and 10th, beginning at 10am Eastern Time both days. At the heart of the sale is an extraordinary opportunity for collectors of American ceramics: more than 100 lots from the Stradling Study Collection -- property from the celebrated New York City antiques dealers Diana and Gary Stradling. The collection launches the first session with over 100 lots of pottery and related material—a remarkable concentration assembled by two dealers whose scholarship, eye and enthusiasm helped shape the American ceramics market for decades. “Nye & Company is thrilled to bring The Stradling Study Collection to market in partnership with Connor Rush of SFR Antiques, whose assistance and scholarship were instrumental in completing the

title: Scattered masterpieces reunited to highlight legacy of pre-1945 German-Jewish collectors
summary: The exhibition From Monet to Picasso. Jewish Art Collectors in Germany reconstructs fifteen major collections of modern art built up by German Jews before 1945, and thus reunites works now scattered all over the world. Not only does it showcase outstanding early modern art works, but also presents historical documents to trace their journeys and the lives of their former owners. The fate of the collectors during the Shoah as well as the associated dissolution of their collections are essential elements in the show’s conceptual design. The exhibition commemorates the pioneering role of German Jews in establishing, fostering and defending modern forms of art in Germany. The works on show range from the time of Realism and Impressionism to Expressionism and New Objectivity. title: Julien's Auctions to present personal items of Dave Brubeck and Tony Bennett
summary: Julien’s Auctions presents Jazz Legends, a landmark two-day auction celebrating the enduring legacies of jazz icons Dave Brubeck and Tony Bennett. Taking place September 17-18 from Los Angeles, the sale features more than 200 personal items from the Estate of Dave Brubeck along with more than 180 artworks by the beloved singer and painter Tony Bennett. Dave Brubeck, honored as a “Living Legend” by the Library of Congress, was a cornerstone of both the jazz and classical music scenes. Across a vibrant career spanning six decades, his creative use of odd time signatures, polyrhythms, polytonality, and improvised counterpoint defined his groundbreaking approach to music. title: Hollywood actress's antique art glass in auction
summary: The collection of hundreds of French and American art glass treasures from the estate of former fashion model and prolific 1950s and 1960s film and television actress, Lori Nelson (1933-2020), will be offered at auction in Los Angeles and online by Goldberg Coins & Collectibles on October 8, 2026. The collection includes art glass by Tiffany, Gallé, Steuben, Daum Nancy, and other prominent artists of the 19th and early 20th centuries. “Before, during, and after her career with Universal Pictures, Lori Nelson was a passionate collector who assembled one of the largest private collections of French and American art glass. She took extreme care to preserve and secure her treasures. In fact, because of the precautions she took, all but one of her more than 300 art glass items safely survived intact the 6.7 magnitude Northridge earthquake that shook Los Angeles in 1994,” said Freeman Fisher, Goldberg Coins & Collectibles Director of Collectibles. “There are many museum-qualit

title: Mexico's paleontologists call for stronger protection of fossils at 37th FILAH
summary: Fossils may be millions of years old, but the questions surrounding their protection are very much of the present. At the recently concluded 37th International Anthropology and History Book Fair (FILAH) in Mexico City, paleontologists and researchers used a public discussion and a new exhibition to look at how Mexico has advanced in safeguarding its fossil heritage — and at the work that still remains to be done. Held at the National Museum of Anthropology, the discussion brought together specialists from the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) and the National Autonomous University of Mexico to consider the scientific, legal and social challenges facing paleontology in the country. Among the participants were Eduardo Corona Martínez, president of INAH’s Paleontology Council; Felisa Aguilar Arellano, academic coordinator of the Quinametzin Paleontological Research Center; and Elena Centeno García of UNAM’s Institute of Geology. title: Fergus McCaffrey to present Paul Wallach's first Asian exhibition in Tokyo
summary: Fergus McCaffrey will present DIVISIBLE, an exhibition of recent sculpture by Paul Wallach (b. 1960), opening September 12 at its Tokyo gallery — his first exhibition in Asia. The artist will be present at the opening. Following a celebrated return to New York in 2025 after three decades shown largely in Europe and more than thirty years working resolutely from Paris, Wallach has built one of the more singular sculptural practices of his generation. It is a body of work that moves fluently between the intimacy of a small, hand-worked wall piece and the permanent, outdoor scale of a public installation, without ever losing the same exacting, personal logic. His is a voice that has grown in influence while never asking to be noticed — a discreet, essential presence in the wider field of sculpture today. title: Light installations by Marinella Senatore and ALP Summer Laboratory in St. Moritz
summary: As part of the newly founded art programme REFLECTION, the award-winning Italian artist Marinella Senatore will present a set of new site-specific light installations (Luminarie) entitled I Contain Multitudes in St. Moritz, Switzerland, from late August until October 2026. The installations will be shown at Schulhausplatz and Forum Paracelsus. REFLECTION is a public art programme that places site-specific works in dialogue with their surroundings and in relation to the people of St. Moritz. It is the first major project initiated by the newly established Kulturstiftung St. Moritz (St. Moritz Cultural Foundation) itself. Beginning in 2026, artists will be invited every two years to spend time in residence in St. Moritz. Drawing on the experiences, traces and inspirations encountered during their stay, the resulting artworks are intended to enter into dialogue with the urban and alpine landscape, whether temporarily or permanently. title: New digital archive highlights work of Italian artist Augusto Salvatore Oppo
summary: A new open digital archive is bringing renewed attention to Augusto Salvatore Oppo (Sassari, 1939–2015), an Italian painter, designer and educator whose work developed over more than five decades but remained largely outside the national art-historical narrative. Created by the artist's sons, Paolo and Carlo Oppo, the Augusto Oppo Archive has already documented more than 500 works and continues to expand as paintings, documents, photographs and testimonies emerge from private collections, homes and archives. The project is not conceived as a closed retrospective catalogue. Its public and participatory structure is central to the research: collectors and private owners are invited to submit information and photographs of works that have not yet been documented. Publishing the archive has itself become a means of discovery, gradually reconnecting works that had become geographically and privately dispersed. Oppo was born in Sassari, Sardinia, in 1939. title: New exhibition asks who gets to decide what counts as a masterpiece
summary: Winterthur Museum, Garden & Library's new exhibition, Challenging Masterpieces: Art and Identity in American Furniture, uses more than 70 objects from its own collection to show how the term masterpiece was constructed, who it left out, and how it's being redefined today. Developed by Joshua W. Lane, the Lois F. and Henry S. McNeil Curator of Furniture, the exhibition opens Sept. 26, 2026, and runs through May 2, 2027. Organized around a single question, What makes a masterpiece? the exhibition traces how that label emerged among early 20th-century collectors, hardened into orthodoxy, and is now being reconsidered. The show unfolds across two galleries and two themes: the first traces how the idea of the aesthetic “masterpiece” took hold in American antiques collecting in the early 20th century; the second carries that inquiry forward, showing how the definition has expanded from the 1970s to the present. “We chose the exhibition title to spur reflection on masterpiece a

title: Graciela Iturbide's 1986 East Los Angeles photographs on view at ROSEGALLERY
summary: ROSEGALLERY will present White Fence, Los Cholos, an exhibition of photographs made by Graciela Iturbide in East Los Angeles in 1986. On May 2, 1986, an assignment for the landmark documentary photographic project A Day in the Life of America brought Iturbide to an apartment in the East L.A. neighborhood of Boyle Heights. There, she was welcomed into a household of young men and women connected to the historic White Fence gang. Named for the white picket fence that surrounded La Purísma Catholic Church (the early gathering place for a youth group and sports team formed by a group of young Mexican American men), following the second World War, the White Fence gang developed into one of the most prominent gangs of the twentieth century. When Iturbide arrived, the community was facing not only intense gang violence, but crises of addiction and police brutality. title: Gina Babić turns anatomy, fragility and memory into sculpture at Spazio Iris
summary: For Gina Babić, the human body belongs to two very different worlds. In one, it is something to be studied, understood and treated through her work as an orthopedic doctor. In the other, it becomes material for imagination — something that can be reshaped, distorted and freed from the rules of anatomy. Those two experiences come together in Carni Scelte, Babić’s solo exhibition opening September 4 at Spazio Iris in Spoltore, near Pescara. Curated by Carla Abril Maizon, the exhibition brings ceramics and installations into a conversation about the body, vulnerability and the complicated boundary between professional responsibility and artistic freedom. title: Rowan University MCA presents Diane Burko environmental exhibition
summary: The Rowan University Museum of Contemporary Art presents Diane Burko: Extraction, A Dialogue of Extremes, a multimedia exhibition on view from August 24 through October 17, 2026 at RUMOCA's 301 High Street W. Gallery. An opening reception will be held on Wednesday, September 16, from 5:00–7:00 p.m., preceded by a 4:00 p.m. panel discussion exploring the intersection of art and science. Presented in collaboration with the Arctic Radium Isotope Observing Network (ARION), a National Science Foundation–funded research project led by Rowan University Associate Professor Dr. Lauren E. Kipp and Dr. Matt Charette of the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, the exhibition demonstrates how artistic practice and scientific research can illuminate the environmental challenges shaping our world. title: MCA Australia unveils artist Nell's Loti Smorgon Sculpture Terrace Commission
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA Australia) today unveils the 2026–2027 Loti Smorgon Sculpture Terrace Commission by Sydney-based artist Nell (b. 1975, Maitland, New South Wales). Holding Both (2026) is a life-size bronze sculpture of a woman balancing the weight of two suspended glass ghosts across her shoulders. Timeless and universal, the figure reflects women's physical and emotional capacity to hold two things at once. Nell has been making figurative sculptures of women for nearly two decades, and her new commission has been in development for many years. ‘I’ve been wanting to make this work for over 15 years and have been waiting for the right set of circumstances to create and present it, and the MCA Loti Smorgon Sculpture Terrace is the right time and place', says Nell. title: Lizzadro Museum to present retrospective of award-winning jeweler Mark Schneider
summary: An exhibition of award-winning jeweler Mark Schneider’s one-of-a-kind pieces will open on view at the Lizzadro Museum of Lapidary Art from November 7, 2026-March 28, 2027. The exhibition is guest curated by Elyse Zorn Karlin. Jewelry designer Mark Schneider has won an amazing 68 prestigious jewelry industry awards, no doubt setting a record for an individual designer. Mark ‘grew up’ in his family’s retail jewelry business. In 1981, he had an epiphany—he decided he should pivot into designing his own jewelry. What is special about Mark’s designs is how he begins them. Through his extensive network of gem dealers and gem carvers, he searches for stones that will evolve into his magnificent jewels. title: De Buck returns to Chelsea with month-long pop-up and Armory Show presentation
summary: De Buck will return to Chelsea this September with its first pop-up gallery, taking over a space in the newly redesigned Arts Building at 529 West 20th Street for a month-long program that will mix contemporary artists with modern and secondary-market works. Running from September 3 through October 4, the temporary gallery marks De Buck’s return to a physical space in the neighborhood and will operate more like a changing exhibition than a conventional static presentation. New rotations are planned each week, allowing the gallery to continually reshape the conversation among artists from different generations. The opening installation brings together two generations of Belgian art through works by Gommaar Gilliams and the late Roger Raveel. title: Cité internationale des arts presents To Make Space for the World exhibition
summary: Taking Cité internationale des arts as the starting point, To Make Space for the World proposes a wider reflection on how contemporary artists address the promises, contradictions and afterlives of cultural internationalism, a form of exchange, action, and solidarity that extends beyond national frameworks. Bringing together 16 artists from 15 different countries (in residence between 2003 and the present day), To Make Space for the World presents the relation to borders, known as the international, not as a settled value, but as something lived unevenly: a daily process of negotiation, translation, hospitality and forced displacement for many; a structure of opportunity, but also of dependence; a promise that could orient artists powerfully, while never entirely escaping the political and cultural asymmetries of the world around it. title: Pioneering new study reveals the deadly impacts of plastic pollution on wildlife populations for the first time
summary: Mounting levels of plastic waste in the environment are affecting wildlife populations, new research has revealed. Every year, around 50 million tonnes of plastic is dumped into the environment. This waste entangles, chokes and poisons wildlife across the world, including sable shearwaters living on the remote Australian island of Lord Howe. After hatching on the island, these birds head out to sea for several years before returning to breed as adults. Sable shearwaters have rapidly become some of the most plastic-polluted animals in the world, with parents known to feed their chicks waste after mistaking it for food. The devastating impacts of this mean many chicks experience dementia-like symptoms and suffer from a fibrotic disease known as ‘plasticosis’. title: New Ilmin Museum show explores contemporary abstraction and mood
summary: Ilmin Museum of Art is presenting Vibe Era, a group exhibition on view from August 26 to October 25, 2026. In an age where a convincing mood or effect replaces aesthetic judgment and form, Vibe Era explores contemporary abstraction and its images as precursors to such transformations. Like evolving organisms seeking unresolved forms, the participating artists—Park Rim, Park Junghae, Park Hyunjung, and Han Jihyoung—experiment with abstraction amid the continuity between a past lost in its making and the future it points toward. Over the past decade, abstract art has been challenged from two directions. The first concerns its aesthetic legitimacy. title: Prague's enfant terrible of contemporary art brings his most iconic works to London
summary: A new exhibition by Czech artist David Černý — one of the most renowned visual artists of his generation and influential creator of Prague’s public space — opens in London on 12 September, showcasing the artist’s most notable works from the 1990s. The works will be on display as models reprinted in 3D by the globally successful Czech company Prusa Research. The exhibition is presented as part of the London Design Festival and the 30th Made in Prague Festival organised by the Czech Centre. Černý, whose push-up making double-decker became a sensation during the 2012 London Olympics, will attend the opening of his solo London exhibition. title: Microscopic grains reveal global stories in Berlin exhibition on sand
summary: Sand, one of the most ordinary materials underfoot, becomes a subject of close scrutiny and unexpected beauty in “To See the World in a Grain of Sand,” an exhibition bringing together the work of Matthias Burba and Max Seeger at the Alfred Ehrhardt Stiftung in Berlin. The exhibition remains on view through September 6, 2026. At its center are the microphotographs of Matthias Burba, born in 1954, a forensic scientist and synesthete who has assembled a collection of roughly 800 sand samples from locations around the world. Seen through a polarizing microscope, the grains lose their familiar appearance and become vivid compositions of color, texture, and fractured light.
